units.meaning: The purpose of 8 FAM 801.2 is to provide guidance concerning the use of information request letters (IRLs) and information notices (INs).

Information request letters (IRLs) are defined as personalized, standardized letters containing a date and signature block that request additional information, documentation, or action needed from the applicant to process a passport application.
Before suspending an application, the adjudicator must fully adjudicate the application to ensure that all issues are addressed.
IRLs are carefully crafted to clearly and accurately communicate statutory, regulatory, and other Department requirements.

Passport agencies and centers are prohibited from making unilateral changes or alterations to IRLs without approval from the Office of Adjudication (CA/PPT/S/A), except in extenuating circumstances on a case-by-case basis with the approval of passport agency or center management (such as when requesting a birth certificate instead of a notification of birth registration and the applicant insists that the notification is the birth certificate).
Posts must use the cleared language in IRLs.
Posts are authorized to modify the cleared language of IRLs to suit local logistical requirements and other local concerns, such as available documentation.
IRLs do not constitute adjudicative guidance.
A passport application must be adjudicated in accordance with 8 FAM before selecting the appropriate IRL to address any deficiencies related to the passport or Consular Report of Birth Abroad (CRBA).
Information notices (INs) are standardized notices that provide passport bearers with information concerning their passports.
An IN may be included to explain why a passport was limited in validity, what documentation is needed to obtain a fully valid passport, or both.
INs are carefully crafted to communicate passport information clearly and accurately.

Passport agencies and centers are prohibited from making unilateral changes or alterations to INs without CA/PPT/S/A approval, except in extenuating circumstances on a case-by-case basis with the approval of passport agency or center management (such as when using endorsement 46 to limit a passport for a special problem).
INs do not require an applicant response and do not need to be personalized with the applicant's name and address.
When tailoring correspondence to a specific situation, posts may consult Passport Services' IRL index and IN index, or contact AskPPTAdjudication@state.gov.
